vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Off, so that a vulnerability fix rides in the one weekly pull request like every other raise instead of arriving as its own. The default would open one per advisory, on its own branch, outside the schedule.

lockFileMaintenance.description: The second pull request of the week, the day after the first: bun.lock and uv.lock regenerated, which is where the transitive dependencies move. Nothing this repository names changes in it, which is why it is not folded into the first.

packageRules.description: One pull request for everything, majors and vulnerability fixes included (separateMajorMinor and vulnerabilityAlerts are off for that). Every version here is pinned exactly and every check has to be green before anything merges, so a week's updates arriving as separate pull requests is that many rounds of CI to land one week's work.
engines.bun is the floor a contributor's machine has to clear, not a pin, and it moves only when the code starts needing something newer.

customManagers.description: A version with the SHA-256 or SHA-512 of the file it names on the next line: Bun, uv, actionlint and the engine. The tag and the digest move together, and the datasource finds the new digest in the checksum file the release publishes.

A tag with the commit it names on the next line, for a repository fetched as an archive of that commit: gdUnit4. The archive's own digest sits under it and is rewritten by hand when the raise fails, as the installer says.
The runner images inside a job matrix, which the github-actions manager reads from runs-on: but not from a matrix.
The Node the release job sets up, which is there only for the npm that comes with it: trusted publishing needs a newer one than the runner ships.
